subject.title: feat: Let users steer running ACP/sub-agent sessions from Discord (and other chat surfaces)

question: Should ordinary Discord and bound ACP thread messages bypass busy reply-operation/channel admission to reach active-run queue policy by default, and should #89238 or a successor be the canonical implementation path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the durable routing contract affects message ordering, session-state ownership, and fallback semantics that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Refresh the admission PR
options.body: Use #89238 as the canonical path or replace it with a rebased branch that preserves stale-operation recovery and makes accepted queue-policy turns distinguishable from empty visible replies.

options.title: Limit steering to explicit controls
options.body: Keep ordinary messages queued for now and document command-only steering until maintainers choose a safer active-session ingress design.

options.title: Split Discord ACP tracking
options.body: Keep #48003 as the broader canonical steering bug and track a narrower Discord ACP/thread issue only if that surface needs separate ownership.

recommendation.title: Refresh the admission PR
recommendation.body: Use #89238 as the canonical path or replace it with a rebased branch that preserves stale-operation recovery and makes accepted queue-policy turns distinguishable from empty visible replies.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision sits in the current reply admission and session-state paths he most recently touched on main.
